from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors extend beyond simple geometric arrows.",
            "Objects are vectors if they follow specific rules.",
            "We study addition and scaling behavior.",
            "Abstract spaces mirror intuitive vector movement.",
            "A set becomes a space via these rules."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Mobjects for animation
        vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*1.5 + RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        abstract_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        abstract_space = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF00FF").move_to(self.grid[pos]) for pos in ["B2", "B4", "C3", "D2", "D4"]])
        arrows = VGroup(
            Arrow(abstract_space[0].get_center(), abstract_space[1].get_center(), color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1),
            Arrow(abstract_space[2].get_center(), abstract_space[3].get_center(), color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(vector))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        new_dot = self.place_at_grid(abstract_dot.copy(), 'C3', scale_factor=2)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(vector, new_dot))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(abstract_space))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Create(arrows))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(abstract_space), FadeOut(arrows), FadeOut(new_dot))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Non-Geometric Examples: Polynomials", [
            "Polynomials can act like vectors.", 
            "Adding polynomials mirrors vector addition.", 
            "Scaling preserves the polynomial's degree."
        ])
        
        # Polynomial P(x) = ax^2 + bx + c
        poly = MathTex("P(x) = a", "x^2", "+", "b", "x", "+", "c")
        self.place_at_grid(poly, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Vector version
        vec = MathTex("\\vec{v} = \\begin{bmatrix} a \\\\ b \\\\ c \\end{bmatrix}")
        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(poly))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight coefficients a, b, c
        self.play(
            Indicate(poly[1:2], color="#FFFF00"),
            Indicate(poly[4:5], color="#FFFF00"),
            Indicate(poly[6:7], color="#FFFF00"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show them behaving like a vector
        self.play(Write(vec))
        self.play(
            poly[1:2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            poly[4:5].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            poly[6:7].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            vec.animate.set_color("#00FF00")
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Closure is the primary test.", "Operations must stay within the set.", "Violating closure breaks the space."]
        self.setup_layout("Verification Logic: The 'Closed' Test", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        box = Rectangle(width=3, height=3, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(box, "B2", "D4")
        label = Text("Closed Set", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        label.next_to(box, UP)
        
        element = Dot(color=PURPLE, radius=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(element, "C3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(box), Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(element))
        self.play(element.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Indicate staying inside
        self.play(element.animate.set_color("#00FF00").scale(1.2))
        self.play(element.animate.set_color("#00FF00").scale(1/1.2))
        self.wait(1)

sections.title: From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition
sections.content: Briefly revisit Euclidean space (R², R³) using a grid animation. Introduce the concept that vectors aren't just 'arrows'; they are objects that follow specific rules (addition and scaling). Define the 'Abstract' shift: if a set follows these 8 rules, it behaves like a vector space.
sections.example: Visualize a 2D coordinate plane morphing into a collection of abstract 'objects' (like polynomial functions) that follow the same parallel-grid movement logic.

sections.title: The Golden Rules: Axioms of a Vector Space
sections.content: Categorize the 8 axioms into two pillars: 1. Additive structure (Commutativity, Associativity, Identity, Inverse) and 2. Scalar multiplication structure (Distributivity, Identity). Use a visual checklist where each rule 'clicks' into a structure icon.
sections.example: Use a simple 'Robot Assembly' analogy: 'Addition' is combining parts, and 'Scalar Multiplication' is resizing a part. If the robot parts follow the rules, they form a valid vector space.

sections.title: Non-Geometric Examples: Polynomials
sections.content: Demonstrate that the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ n satisfies the axioms. Use an animation showing how adding two polynomials (like 2x + 1 and x² + 3) mirrors the vector addition logic (combining coefficients as components).
sections.example: Imagine two 'DNA sequences' (represented as polynomials). Show that if we add them or scale them, the resulting object still lives within the 'Polynomial World'.

sections.title: Verification Logic: The 'Closed' Test
sections.content: Establish the most critical practical test: Closure under Addition and Scalar Multiplication. Use a visual 'Boundary Test'—if an operation keeps the object inside the defined 'space,' it passes.
sections.example: A filter device: Inputs are fed in; if the filter changes the nature of the object (e.g., adding a constant that forces a degree higher than n), it is NOT a vector space.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Abstract vector spaces allow us to use geometric intuition (distance, projection, orthogonality) on non-geometric data (functions, matrices, signals).
sections.example: Show a collage of a 3D arrow, a wave function, and a matrix, all connected by a single glowing 'Vector Space' thread to signify they share the same mathematical DNA.
